rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "W = F.d; tau = r x F with magnitude = moment arm x force; L = r x p is conserved when net torque vanishes."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The hinge theorem*** — a door's handle is far from the hinge because torque scales with r: same push, more turn.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The two products split mechanics: projections (dot) earn energy, perpendiculars (cross) turn things - cos th and sin th are the physics.  ·  Work: W = F.d = F d cos th; scalar, unit joule; zero when F perp d; negative when opposing. Torque: tau = r x F; magnitude r F sin th = moment arm x force; axial vector by right-hand rule; unit N.m; zero when force line passes through the pivot. Angular momentum: L = r x p; conserved when net torque is zero (tau = dL/dt). Parallelogram law of forces: resultant magnitude sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2F1F2 cos alpha).…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Vectors at Work (Literally) Physics runs on the vector products: **work** W = F·d (dot), **torque** τ = r × F (cross), **angular momentum** L = r × p (cross). Each formula is a theorem about components — and each has a syllabus-standard numerical type.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Work — the dot product - **Theorem:** W = **F·d** = |F||d|cos θ = F d cos θ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement. - Only the force component **along** the displacement earns work: W = (F cos θ)d. Perpendicular force does **zero** work (θ = 90°). - SI unit: joule (J = N·m). Sign: positive (assisting), zero (perpendicular), negative (opposing — friction).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Work: F d cos th. Torque magnitude: r F sin th. Component torque: determinant, keep the k-hat for planar forces. Zero cases: perpendicular force (work), force through pivot (torque).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): A force of 10 N acts at 60° to a displacement of 5 m. Find the work done.** — **Formula:** W = **F·d** = F d cos θ, the dot product of force and displacement. **Substitute:** W = 10 × 5 × cos 60° = 50 × ½ = **25 J**.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): A force F = 3î + 4ĵ N acts at a point with position vector r = 2î + ĵ m from the pivot. Find the torque about the pivot.** — **Formula:** τ = **r × F**. **Determinant:** |î ĵ k̂; 2 1 0; 3 4 0| = î[(1)(0) − (0)(4)] − ĵ[(2)(0) − (0)(3)] + k̂[(2)(4) − (1)(3)] = 0î − 0ĵ + **5k̂**.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A planet keeps orbiting because the Sun's force points along r: zero torque, conserved angular momentum - Kepler's second law in one line.

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why dot for work, cross for torque - Work asks "how much force along the motion" — a projection (cos θ, dot). Torque asks "how much force across the lever" — a perpendicular measure (sin θ, cross). The two products split physics between them.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **N·m for torque is not a joule:** same dimensions, different quantity — torque is a vector about an axis, energy a scalar.  ·  **Moment arm is perpendicular distance:** r sin θ, not r — the full radius only works at θ = 90°.  ·  **Negative work is real:** friction doing negative work removes kinetic energy; the sign is information.

rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (3m): A force of 10 N acts at 60° to a displacement of 5 m. Find the work done.** — W = F d cos θ = 10 × 5 × cos 60° = 10 × 5 × ½ = **25 J**. Only the component F cos θ = 5 N along the displacement contributes; the perpendicular 5√3 N component does nothing.  ·  **NEB-style (3m): A force F = 3î + 4ĵ N acts at the point r = 2î + ĵ m relative to a pivot. Find the torque about the pivot.** — τ = r × F = |î ĵ k̂; 2 1 0; 3 4 0| = k̂[(2)(4) − (1)(3)] = **5k̂ N·m** — magnitude 5 N·m, direction out of the plane (right-hand rule).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Why does a door open easiest when pushed at the edge farthest from the hinge?** — Torque τ = r F sin θ: for a fixed force applied perpendicular to the door (sin θ = 1), τ is proportional to **r**, the distance from the hinge.…
